REL-0001.evidence_requirement: Cite the change-class rule table by file:line and paste the linter exit code for three crafted diffs (one per bump class). A claim that the rule is enforced must cite an exit code, not the presence of the rule in a document.
inputs: the formal contract set produced by the specification lane (B06)
the current plugin manifest and marketplace registry entry
git tags and the tag-to-HEAD diff
REL-0001.question_or_target: Implementation target: turn the release policy and versioning rules the spec demands at lines 10817-10820 into a machine-checkable artifact. Enumerate, for the plugin package, the registry entry, the blueprint pack and the CouncilSpec schema, exactly which change classes force MAJOR, MINOR or PATCH -- manifest key removal, permission widening, hook-contract signature change, blueprint id retirement, a schema field becoming required -- then ship a linter that derives the REQUIRED bump from the git diff between the previous tag and HEAD and exits non-zero whenever the declared version is lower than the derived one.
REL-0001.retry_policy: two strikes then pivot (AGENTS.md 4b): after the second failure carrying the same error fingerprint, enumerate at least two mechanically different approaches before any third attempt
REL-0001.reviewer_requirement: one fresh-context adversarial reviewer from the OTHER vendor than this unit's executor; a same-vendor reviewer inherits the executor's blind spots
tests_required: Mutation: delete a required manifest key and declare a PATCH bump -> linter exits non-zero.
Both-states: a genuinely patch-only diff declared as PATCH -> linter silent (no false positive).
Widening a declared tool permission must classify MAJOR even though no key was removed.
A pure file rename with byte-identical content must classify as no-bump-required.
REL-0001.title: Semantic-version contract with a diff-derived bump linter

REL-0006.evidence_requirement: Quote the fetched artifact sha256 alongside the manifest value. Quote the acceptance-probe output before and after. Report MTTR in seconds with the clock source named; an estimated duration is not a measurement.
inputs: the release store holding the N-1 artifact
the N-1 acceptance probe and the upgraded profile left by REL-0005
the typed inverse actions from REL-0002
REL-0006.question_or_target: Implementation target: rehearse going backwards. Check the blocking precondition first -- the N-1 artifact must be fetchable from the release store and its sha256 must equal the value recorded in ROLLBACK-MANIFEST.md, because a plan that assumes an artifact nobody can fetch is not a plan -- then downgrade the canary and prove restoration by re-running the N-1 acceptance probe rather than by reading a version string. Record wall-clock time from decision to restored behaviour as the MTTR figure the runbook will quote.
REL-0006.retry_policy: resumable with mandatory restore: on interruption the profile is rolled back to its captured baseline before the next attempt, and the resume boundary is recorded
REL-0006.reviewer_requirement: one reviewer who re-executes the drill end to end on a freshly created profile from the recorded commands alone; a reviewer who reads the transcript has not rehearsed it
tests_required: Precondition control: corrupt the stored N-1 artifact -> the retrievability gate blocks before any downgrade begins.
Show that a version-string read reports N-1 while behaviour is still N, which is why the behaviour probe is the acceptance signal.
Zero owner-authored files are removed during the downgrade, verified against the pre-downgrade hashes.
MTTR is recorded and compared against the figure the runbook publishes; a divergence fails the drill.
REL-0006.title: Downgrade drill: artifact retrievability precondition, behaviour-restored proof, measured MTTR

REL-0014.evidence_requirement: The receipt carries the artifact sha256, the database snapshot id, the scan timestamp and the window length. A promotion consuming a result outside the window must be visible as a refusal in the log, not merely absent.
inputs: the scanner, pinned, and its advisory database snapshot metadata
any previously stored scan results and their timestamps
REL-0014.question_or_target: Implementation target: make the vulnerability gate decay-aware. A scan result is a query against a live advisory database, so last week's green says nothing about today's advisory set. Implement three properties: re-run the scanner against the exact artifact hash at the moment of promotion, record the advisory-database snapshot identifier and timestamp inside the receipt, and refuse to consume any stored result older than the declared window rather than reusing it.
REL-0014.retry_policy: retry permitted only with a re-pulled advisory database; reusing the cached database makes the second run the same measurement as the first
REL-0014.reviewer_requirement: one reviewer whose sole job is to re-run the mutation controls and confirm each one turns the gate red; a reviewer who only re-reads the result has verified nothing
tests_required: Feed a stored result older than the window -> the gate refuses to consume it and forces a re-scan.
Detector control: pin a dependency with a known advisory -> the scanner reports it.
A scanner exiting non-zero for a tooling reason classifies NOT-CHECKED; the estate has a measured case where exit 127 was read as a clean scan.
Two runs minutes apart must both record their own snapshot id; a reused id fails the freshness check.
REL-0014.title: Advisory re-scan at the promotion moment with an enforced freshness window

REL-0017.evidence_requirement: Show the dry-run plan and the applied diff side by side; they must be identical. State explicitly that the operation ran against a copy, with the copy's path. Report how many source-unique files were preserved versus refused.
inputs: a captured copy of the real hand-managed layout, never the live tree itself
the two-directional divergence measurement from the current-state audit lane (B02)
the typed inverse actions from REL-0002
_USER-PROMPTS.md:10838 (migration from old layouts) and 11306 (repository differs from live)
REL-0017.question_or_target: Implementation target: rehearse converting the pre-plugin hand-managed layout -- loose skills in the live tree, hand-edited hook registrations, rule files modified in place -- into the plugin-managed layout. Work on a copy of a captured real layout, run the conversion in dry-run mode first and require the printed plan to match the applied result exactly, and demonstrate reversibility by restoring from the backup the conversion takes. Where the source holds content the target does not, the conversion must preserve it or refuse: the measured baseline on this estate is 5 of 88 live rule files identical to their repository counterparts, with unique content on both sides, so copying in either direction destroys work.
REL-0017.retry_policy: resumable with mandatory restore: on interruption the profile is rolled back to its captured baseline before the next attempt, and the resume boundary is recorded
REL-0017.reviewer_requirement: one reviewer who must attempt to destroy a planted owner-authored file through any lifecycle path and demonstrate the oracle catches it before signing off
tests_required: Dry-run plan versus applied result: the diff must be empty.
A file existing only in the source layout survives the conversion with its hash intact.
Restore from the conversion's own backup returns the tree to its exact pre-conversion hash set.
A file differing only in line endings is classified unchanged, not as a conflict; otherwise every Windows-authored file reads as spurious drift.
REL-0017.title: Legacy hand-managed layout migration, dry-run first, on a copy, refusing one-directional overwrite

REL-0020.evidence_requirement: Enumerate every cache location seeded and every location the probe could not reach, the latter marked NOT-CHECKED. Quote the behavioural output that distinguishes old bytes from new bytes; a version string is not that output.
inputs: the cache locations the client consults, enumerated from the client's own resolution order
the previous package used as the poison payload
the candidate package and its refresh step
_USER-PROMPTS.md:11305 (stale cache masks a fixed package) and 10837 (cache refresh)
REL-0020.question_or_target: Implementation target: prove the release's refresh step actually invalidates. Construct the broken state deliberately -- a stale copy of the previous package seeded into every cache location the client consults -- then install the candidate and assert the running client executes the new bytes. Spec line 11305 names the class: a stale cache masking a fixed package. An invalidation test run against an empty cache is silent in the broken state and the fixed state alike, and therefore measures nothing at all.
REL-0020.retry_policy: retry only on a FRESH profile. Re-running a lifecycle drill on a dirtied profile measures the dirt, not the drill; the profile must be destroyed and recreated between attempts
REL-0020.reviewer_requirement: one reviewer whose sole job is to re-run the mutation controls and confirm each one turns the gate red; a reviewer who only re-reads the result has verified nothing
tests_required: With the refresh step disabled the drill must FAIL, proving it can perceive the defect.
With the refresh step enabled and the cache poisoned, the client executes the new behaviour.
Show that a version-string read reports the new version while poisoned old bytes still execute.
Any cache location not covered appears as NOT-CHECKED rather than being omitted from the receipt.
REL-0020.title: Cache invalidation proved from the poisoned state, not the empty one

REL-0021.evidence_requirement: Report the four-way classification counts: identical, package-only, deployed-only, and divergent-both-ways. Name the retrieval command used for the blob and show the measured CRLF count difference against the rejected alternative, so the recipe choice is evidenced rather than asserted.
inputs: the git object store at the promotion commit
the deployed tree the package claims to represent
the two-directional divergence baseline from the current-state audit lane (B02)
REL-0021.question_or_target: Implementation target: before promoting, prove the three copies of every shipped file agree. Compare, per file, the git blob obtained with git cat-file (never git archive, which on this box hands back CRLF worktree bytes instead of the blob), the bytes inside the built package, and the bytes in the deployed tree, normalising line endings before comparison so that end-of-line noise cannot masquerade as content drift. Block when the deployed copy and the repository copy each hold unique content, because that is the two-directional case where reconciling in either direction destroys work.
REL-0021.retry_policy: zero retries. The first observation IS the verdict; a later disagreeing run is recorded as a discrepancy (spec 11039), never retried away
REL-0021.reviewer_requirement: one reviewer who must attempt to destroy a planted owner-authored file through any lifecycle path and demonstrate the oracle catches it before signing off
tests_required: Run git archive and git cat-file on one known file and record the differing CRLF counts, justifying the chosen recipe.
A file present only in the deployed tree classifies as deployed-only, not as missing.
A file differing only in line endings classifies as identical.
A planted two-directional divergence produces BLOCK, never a one-directional sync proposal.
REL-0021.title: Three-way byte parity between git blob, packaged copy and deployed copy

REL-0022.evidence_requirement: State what the observer can and cannot perceive -- side effects produced by a spawned child process, for instance -- and mark the blind region NOT-CHECKED. A zero-hole finding is only as wide as the observer's demonstrated reach, and that reach must be shown before the finding is stated.
inputs: the system-level observer and the measured limits of what it can see
the installer under test, run inside the canary profile
the recorded inverse set standardised by REL-0002
REL-0022.question_or_target: Implementation target: find out what the recorded recovery plan does NOT cover, by watching the installer run instead of by reading the plan. Attach a system-level observer to a genuine install so each side effect it produces is captured as it happens, then subtract the recorded inverse set from the observed side-effect set in both directions. Anything observed but unrecorded is a recovery hole; anything recorded but never observed is a stale entry that will send the next responder somewhere nothing happened. Coverage inferred from reading a document is not coverage.
REL-0022.retry_policy: retry only on a FRESH profile. Re-running a lifecycle drill on a dirtied profile measures the dirt, not the drill; the profile must be destroyed and recreated between attempts
REL-0022.reviewer_requirement: one reviewer whose sole job is to re-run the mutation controls and confirm each one turns the gate red; a reviewer who only re-reads the result has verified nothing
tests_required: Detector control: produce a known side effect and confirm the observer captures it, before any zero-hole finding is entertained.
Introduce an unrecorded side effect into the installer -> the subtraction reports a hole.
Remove a real side effect while leaving its recorded inverse -> the stale-entry direction fires.
Side effects produced by a child process are either captured or declared an uncovered region.
REL-0022.title: Rollback coverage measured by instrumenting a real install, not by reading the manifest
